name: P ZERO Race 4S (tube type)

origin.basis: Italian tire maker; Pirelli says the P ZERO Race range is made at its plant in Italy near its Milan headquarters.

manufacturing.basis: The P ZERO Race 4S page does not state where it is made.

positioning: Tube-type all-season P ZERO Race, successor of the P ZERO Velo 4S.
pressure_note: The product page gives no maximum pressure; use the figure printed on the tire.

wet_notes.summary: Pirelli says the SmartEVO compound enhances performance on wet and cold tarmac.

availability.note: Listed in Pirelli's UK catalogue with a dealer finder; P ZERO tires are sold by retail shops on Taobao and Tmall in mainland China; North American availability not verified.

caveats: Lab rolling resistance is with a butyl tube.

image.shown: P ZERO Race 4S tube-type sidewall as pictured in Pirelli's catalogue; one photo covers every width.
image.alt: Close-up of a Pirelli P ZERO Race 4S tube-type road tire sidewall

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other. A 4S owner on the P ZERO Race TLR test who does not state the construction is not counted.

reports.summary: Fast and grippy over a couple of rides, and easy to fit.
Rolls well with amazing grip in wet weather, but five of six rides with TPU tubes ended in punctures on debris-strewn lanes.
Happy in all conditions, with the grip of the Corsa Pro and better endurance.
Loads of grip, rolls nicely and seems to be holding up well.
Easy to fit, with top-end rolling and grip.
Performed superbly over a 1,500 km end-to-end ride with no punctures.
Six months in very wet mountains: grippy, quite fast and no flats, with surprisingly good cut resistance; less supple than a Corsa but much tougher.
